$comment: Tests written ahead of their feature: each must FAIL until the feature is in, then come off this list. See tests/README.md (red first). Only new tests belong here; the floor guard refuses an existing test listed as pending.

pending.test: landing: the scene gains a landing 146 art px wide left of the deck, and the deck moves right with it
landing: four islands, one a seat, each centred on an eighth of the deck's height, with water all round it
landing: the stage is wider by the landing alone, and a maximised window keeps the board's scale on every size
landing: each seat's lantern hangs over the channel by its island, lit on that seat's turn and dark otherwise; an open seat has none
landing: the turn boat is moored under the current seat's lantern with the round on its sign, and has left the wide river
landing: on a turn the boat glides from the last seat's island to the next one, and is simply there with reduced motion
landing: lanterns drift round the islands on loops of their own, never over an island or the deck, each loop closing in LANDING_LOOP
landing: the drifting lanterns are drawn where they float on the scene's ambient clock, and light the water round them
landing: the players sit on four islands left of the board, one a seat in turn order, and the sidebar opens with the weather
landing: each island's grid runs edge to edge, the digit and both stones on its crossings, the captures and the Kata on its lines
landing: the longest name the server allows stays whole on one line, on its island
landing: a passed or away seat fades its stones and name, its stamp on the name's line, its plates solid over the grid
landing: a seat's captures tip opens beside its island, over the water, not over the island or the sidebar
landing: the boat is moored at the seat whose turn it is with the round, that seat's lantern lit, and the header says only YOUR TURN
stage: the hand and the lines under it sit below the deck, left aligned with the scene past the islands
stage: a full hand stays under the deck, its cards overlapping when they don't fit
